requirements.text: We led a seed stage financing for a company still in stealth (can't disclose too many details publicly) but they are hiring their first Infrastructure engineer. You'd be the categorical hire at the company. This is a hands-on, early-stage IC role for someone who has built infrastructure from scratch and wants to work in person in San Francisco, directly partnering with founders and investors at Greylock.
5+ years building backend or infrastructure systems, ideally with a mix of deep infra (control planes, high-availability services) and product-facing platform work.
Hands-on experience with security and privacy engineering: encryption, key management, data isolation, or enterprise compliance requirements.
Experience designing distributed systems, including event-driven or streaming architectures such as Kafka, with a focus on reliability and latency.
Strong skills in a typed backend language (Go, Python, Java or similar) and service-oriented architectures with defined interfaces (gRPC/protobuf).
Experience operating and scaling relational databases (Postgres), including migrations, sharding and cost optimization.
A record of technical leadership: you’ve scoped ambiguous projects, led other engineers, and worked directly with customers or partners to land them.
Comfort owning problems end to end at a scaling company, from design and rollout to on-call.
